glossary.def: Wrapping an agent as a function tool of another agent in the same process. Simple and fast, but couples releases and trust.
Three reply styles. Message-only agents always send messages, task-generating agents always create tasks, and hybrid agents use messages to scope work and a task for committed work.
A task in a terminal state cannot restart. Refinements start a new task in the same `contextId`, optionally with `referenceTaskIds`.
A message field listing earlier tasks that give context for a follow-up or refinement.
A `SendMessageConfiguration` flag. False (default) blocks until the task is terminal or interrupted. True returns the task at once.
The operation that reattaches to a task's event stream. It begins with the current `Task` snapshot.
The wrapper for streamed and pushed updates. It holds exactly one of `task`, `message`, `statusUpdate` or `artifactUpdate`.
The `AUTH_REQUIRED` flow where an agent asks the client for a credential mid-task. The state itself authorizes nothing.
The Foundry role that grants an identity least-privilege access to call agent endpoints, including incoming A2A, without permission to create or change agents.
The generally available Foundry tool type for calling a remote A2A 1.0 agent through a project connection. `a2a_preview` targets 0.3 and is Preview.

claims.text: A2A v1.0.0 was released on 2026-03-12 and the patch v1.0.1 on 2026-05-28.
Google created A2A in April 2025 and the Linux Foundation launched the A2A project on 2025-06-23, citing more than 100 supporting companies.
The specification page header still reads Latest Released Version 1.0.0 (checked 2026-10-13).
The A2A documentation calls wrapping agents as tools inefficient and says A2A exposes agents as they are, with no wrapping.
MCP is vertical (agent to tools and resources) and A2A is horizontal (agent to agent), and the two are complementary.

Agent Framework guidance: use agents as tools when agents share a process and team, and A2A across service, team or organization boundaries, accepting network latency and distributed-service concerns.
An MCP tool call has no task lifecycle unless the Tasks extension is supported.
An Agent Card is served at /.well-known/agent-card.json.
The v1.0 Agent Card requires name, description, supportedInterfaces, version, capabilities, defaultInputModes, defaultOutputModes and skills.
supportedInterfaces is ordered with the first entry preferred, and each entry has url, protocolBinding, protocolVersion and an optional tenant.
Agent Cards may be signed as a JWS (RFC 7515) over the RFC 8785 canonical form, excluding the signatures field.
Agent Card endpoints SHOULD send Cache-Control max-age and an ETag, and clients SHOULD use conditional requests.
The current A2A specification does not prescribe a standard API for curated agent registries.
A Foundry agent's card requires Microsoft Entra authentication and uses the path agentCard/v1.0, and anonymous card access is not supported.
TaskState has nine values: UNSPECIFIED, SUBMITTED, WORKING, four terminal (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED) and two interrupted (INPUT_REQUIRED, AUTH_REQUIRED).
A terminal task cannot restart, so refinements start a new task in the same contextId, optionally with referenceTaskIds.
Task ids are server-generated, client-provided ids for new tasks are not supported, and messages with mismatching contextId and taskId are rejected.
A Part holds exactly one of text, raw, url or data, plus mediaType, filename and metadata.
Messages SHOULD NOT deliver task outputs, which SHOULD be Artifacts, and messages are not a reliable delivery mechanism because they may not be persisted.
TaskArtifactUpdateEvent has append and lastChunk fields so large artifacts can stream in chunks.
A2A defines three functionally equivalent bindings (JSON-RPC, gRPC, HTTP+JSON), and the v1.0.1 patch says HTTP+JSON SHOULD use application/a2a+json.
Clients send A2A-Version as Major.Minor, an empty header means 0.3 and an unsupported version returns VersionNotSupportedError.
Foundry incoming A2A for v1.0 supports only the JSON-RPC binding, text modality and no streaming.
The Agent Framework .NET A2A client prefers HTTP+JSON over JSON-RPC by default and offers A2AClientOptions.PreferredBindings to override it.
SendMessageConfiguration.returnImmediately defaults to false, so SendMessage waits until the task is terminal or interrupted.
SubscribeToTask returns the current Task as the first event and its stream terminates when the task reaches a terminal state.
Streaming needs capabilities.streaming and push notifications need capabilities.pushNotifications on the Agent Card.
Agents SHOULD use a webhook timeout of 10 to 30 seconds and SHOULD NOT blindly post to client-supplied URLs because of SSRF risk.
Agents MUST NOT treat the TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED transition by itself as authorization for any operation.
Foundry retains A2A tasks and contexts for 60 days from their most recent write, and each write resets the period.
Agent Framework A2AAgent keeps context_id, task_id and task_state in the session and returns a continuation token for long-running tasks.
A2A payloads carry no identity, the server MUST authenticate every request, production MUST use TLS, and the spec recommends TLS 1.3 or newer while the enterprise guide says TLS 1.2 or higher.
Incoming A2A on Foundry requires Microsoft Entra authentication and the Foundry Agent Consumer role (or a role granting endpoint access), and key-based or anonymous access is not supported.
The spec marks the implicit and password OAuth flows as Deprecated, while the v1.0 migration page says they were removed.
The Foundry a2a tool type targets A2A 1.0 and is GA, a2a_preview targets 0.3 and is Preview, and the Connected Agents tool is not available in the new Foundry Agent Service.
Foundry serves A2A 0.3 when no A2A-Version header or a2a-version query value is sent, and a header and query value that disagree return HTTP 400.
Agent Framework hosts A2A in .NET with MapA2AHttpJson and MapWellKnownAgentCard and in Python with A2AExecutor built on a2a-sdk, and the packages are prerelease (--prerelease or --pre).
In python-1.4.0 (2026-05-14) agent-framework-a2a migrated to a2a-sdk v1.0.
